Chapter 4

Temporary Speed Reduction & Emission Zones

The special RVV rules for a serious oil-supply disruption, low-emission zones and zero-emission zones in the Netherlands.

  • RVV Chapter VA — Oil-Supply Disruption
  • RVV Chapter VB — Emission Zones

This theory chapter combines two special parts of the RVV 1990. RVV Chapter VA contains a contingency rule for temporarily reducing the maximum speed on motorways and autowegen during a serious disruption of the oil supply. RVV Chapter VB contains the national legal framework for milieuzones and zero-emission zones.

These are not ordinary default traffic rules. They apply only when the legal conditions for the relevant measure or zone are met, so always pay attention to the applicable traffic signs, supplementary plates and current access rules.

§ 1 — Temporary Speed Reduction During an Oil-Supply Disruption

RVV Articles 86a and 86b: a special national contingency rule for autosnelwegen and autowegen.

When Can the Rule Be Activated? Article 86a

In the event of a serious disruption of the oil supply, a ministerial regulation may impose a temporary maximum speed of 90 km/h on autosnelwegen (motorways) and autowegen.

This is a specific statutory emergency provision. It is not a general power to change every speed limit on every road in the Netherlands.

The Special Limit Is 90 km/h

If Article 86a is activated, the special maximum applies on motorways and autowegen to the motor vehicles covered by the provision.

90
Special maximum under Article 86a

Do not learn “130 → 100” as the emergency rule. The RVV provision itself specifies 90 km/h.

Which Vehicles Are Covered? Important exception

The Article 86a reduction does not apply to trucks, motor vehicles towing a trailer, or buses other than T100 buses. Those vehicle categories already have their own maximum-speed rules.

Article 86b makes it an offence for drivers of the motor vehicles covered by Article 86a to exceed the temporary maximum speed set under that provision.

How Long Can It Last? Temporary by law

The ministerial regulation is temporary. Under Article 86a, it must expire no later than the first day of the fifth calendar month after it takes effect.

The regulation is adopted by the responsible minister in agreement with the ministers responsible for justice and economic affairs. Its effective date and legal operation follow the published ministerial regulation.

Study Point

Remember the legal structure: serious oil-supply disruption → ministerial regulation → 90 km/h on motorways and autowegen for the vehicles covered by Article 86a → temporary duration.

§ 2 — Milieuzones & Zero-Emission Zones

RVV Articles 86c–86e: nationally defined access rules that municipalities can apply to designated zones.

The Legal Framework RVV Chapter VB

Municipalities can establish emission zones through traffic decisions, but the vehicle categories, emission classes, signs and statutory exemptions are governed by the national RVV framework.

Since 2026, the main zone sign is C22e. Supplementary plates beneath it show whether the restriction is a milieuzone, a zero-emission zone, which vehicle categories are affected and, for a milieuzone, which diesel emission classes are excluded. The end of the zone is indicated with C22f.

Two Different Zone Systems

🌿
Milieuzone

A milieuzone is a low-emission zone. Under the national RVV rules, the restriction concerns diesel passenger cars, vans, trucks and/or buses, depending on the supplementary plate used by the municipality.

The Dutch system uses standard emission-class thresholds. For passenger cars and vans, a green zone allows diesel emission class 4 and higher, while a blue zone allows class 5 and higher. For diesel trucks and buses, the purple standard requires emission class 6.

  • Applies only to the vehicle categories shown on the supplementary plate
  • Petrol, LPG and electric vehicles are not excluded by the national milieuzone rules merely because of their fuel type
  • Always check the sign and the current emission class of the vehicle
⚡
Zero-Emission Zone

A zero-emission zone under Article 86e applies to vans (bedrijfsauto’s) and trucks (vrachtauto’s). Passenger cars and motorcycles are not covered by the current national zero-emission-zone rule.

The long-term rule is zero tailpipe emissions. Battery-electric and hydrogen vehicles can therefore qualify as zero-emission vehicles. Existing combustion-engine vans and trucks may still have temporary access under transition rules, statutory exemptions or a valid exemption permit.

  • Do not assume that every petrol or diesel vehicle is already banned today
  • Transition rules depend on vehicle type, emission class and first-registration date
  • Use the current official registration/checking service before entering
Milieuzone: Who Is Restricted? Article 86d

Article 86d applies the milieuzone restriction to diesel-powered passenger cars, vans, trucks or buses, but only for the categories and emission classes indicated by the applicable C22e supplementary plate.

This means the older wording “all combustion-engine vehicles are restricted” is incorrect for a milieuzone. The national milieuzone framework is specifically based on diesel vehicles and their emission class.

Zero-Emission Zone: Who Is Restricted? Article 86e

The zero-emission-zone restriction applies to vans and trucks, except zero-emission vehicles. The law also contains transitional access for specified existing vehicles and statutory exceptions for certain categories.

For study purposes, the most important distinction is simple: milieuzone = emission-class restriction for specified diesel vehicles; zero-emission zone = zero-emission requirement for vans and trucks, subject to transition rules and exceptions.

Statutory Exemptions and Special Cases

♿ Wheelchair-accessible vehicles

Wheelchair-accessible passenger cars or vans identified by the relevant registration codes are exempt under the RVV provisions that apply to emission zones.

🏛️ Vehicles 40 years or older

Vehicles whose date of first admission is 40 years or more in the past are included in the statutory exemption framework.

🏕️ Certain camper vans

For a milieuzone, a camper van is exempt where the registered keeper lives inside that milieuzone. Zero-emission-zone treatment depends on the vehicle’s registration category and applicable exemption rules.

🚚 Certain special trucks

Specified special-purpose trucks can qualify for statutory exemptions subject to vehicle codes and age limits. Do not treat every special or commercial vehicle as automatically exempt.

Do Not Memorise a False “Always Exempt” List

The original version of this page incorrectly treated categories such as public transport, military vehicles and all emergency vehicles as a universal automatic exemption list. The legal position is more specific. Exemptions depend on the RVV provision, vehicle registration category, vehicle characteristics and, in some cases, a separate legal basis or permit.

Ontheffing — Exemption Permits Application may be required

An ontheffing is different from an automatic statutory exemption. If a vehicle does not qualify automatically, an exemption permit may be available when the applicable conditions are met.

For zero-emission zones, applications are handled through the central RDW exemption system for the nationally harmonised categories. Examples include day exemptions and specific operational, financial or vehicle-availability situations.

A zero-emission-zone day exemption is generally limited to a maximum of 12 days per vehicle, per municipality, per calendar year. It is valid only for the municipality for which it is issued.
How Zones Are Enforced ANPR commonly used

Many municipalities use automatic number-plate recognition (ANPR) cameras to enforce emission-zone access. Vehicle details can be checked against registration data and exemption records.

Do not describe camera enforcement as the only legally possible method. Municipal enforcement officers may also enforce the restriction. The important rule for drivers is that the restriction applies from the legally indicated zone boundary, not only when a camera is visible.

2026 Zone Signs — How to Recognise Them C22e / C22f

From 2026, milieuzones and zero-emission zones use the same new main sign family. C22e marks entry into a zone where access is restricted because of emission requirements. The supplementary plate underneath tells you which rule applies.

  • Milieuzone: the supplementary plate identifies the affected diesel vehicle category and excluded emission classes.
  • Zero-emission zone: the supplementary plate identifies the zero-emission-zone restriction for vans and trucks.
  • End of zone: C22f marks the end of the emission-zone restriction.

During the 2026 transition, municipalities replaced the older zone signs with the new C22e/C22f system. For current driving, learn the new sign family rather than the former C22a/C22c system.

Milieuzone vs Zero-Emission Zone — Side by Side

FeatureMilieuzoneZero-emission zone
Main purposeKeep specified higher-emitting diesel vehicles out of the zoneMove urban van and truck traffic toward zero tailpipe emissions
Vehicle scopeDiesel passenger cars, vans, trucks and/or buses, as shown on the supplementary plateVans and trucks; passenger cars are not covered by the national ZE-zone rule
Basic access testRequired diesel emission class for the indicated vehicle categoryZero-emission vehicle, or temporary access under a transition rule, exemption or ontheffing
Petrol/LPG passenger carNot excluded by the national milieuzone rulePassenger cars are outside the national ZE-zone rule
Electric / hydrogen vehicleNot restricted as an old diesel vehicleCan qualify as zero-emission if there are no tailpipe emissions
2026 main signC22e + milieuzone supplementary plateC22e + zero-emission supplementary plate
Who decides location?Municipality, through a traffic decision within the national frameworkMunicipality, through a traffic decision within the national framework
Before Entering a Zone

Read the C22e supplementary plate and check the vehicle’s current access status. For a milieuzone, use the official milieuzone/emission-class check. For a zero-emission zone, use the current official zero-emission-zone registration checker and exemption information. Transition dates and permit arrangements can change, so a current check is safer than relying on an old summary.

What Is National and What Is Local?

The legal categories and core access rules are nationally defined in the RVV. A municipality decides whether to introduce a zone, where its boundary lies and which permitted national zone configuration it uses. This is more accurate than saying that every city invents its own emission-class system.

Chapter 4 — What to Take Away

RVV Chapter VA: during a serious oil-supply disruption, a ministerial regulation can temporarily set a 90 km/h maximum on motorways and autowegen for the vehicles covered by Article 86a. The measure is temporary and Article 86b prohibits exceeding that special maximum.

RVV Chapter VB: a milieuzone restricts specified diesel vehicles according to emission class. A zero-emission zone applies to vans and trucks, with transition rules, statutory exemptions and possible ontheffingen. Passenger cars are not covered by the current national zero-emission-zone rule.

For 2026 and later, recognise the C22e/C22f emission-zone sign family and use the supplementary plate to determine exactly which restriction applies.
